svg.title: What is still on the wrong side
svg.desc: Four leftovers of the refactor, each with why it is wrong and which later lesson resolves it.
svg.text: Four things the boundary did NOT sort out, and when each is paid
collect_triangles reads one of its four values; draw_triangles applies the rest
SDL is in the public API
framebuffer says Uint32; gpu_device takes an SDL_Window*. The vocabulary is adopted
render_options ships the demo’s teaching switches
trs_order::tsr exists so a lesson can show a bug. A shipping engine has no such enum
paid in an exercise, and honestly never
splitting it needs an application layer to split it INTO
paid in 5.2, who owns the loop
A refactor lesson that ends “and now it is clean” is lying to you.
The first pass draws the line. Which side each thing belongs on is argued for the rest of the module
— and two of these four are argued by code that does not exist yet.
